stories.title: Investigation launched as ‘diphtheria’ claims life in KP's Bajaur
summary: BAJAUR: The health department on Monday launched measures against suspected diphtheria cases after the infection left a child dead and infected two others in War Mamund tehsil of Bajaur district.
When contacted, District Health Officer Dr Gohar Ayub confirmed to Dawn the death of a girl child and the infection of two others.

He said as per the investigation, the infection was initially reported in the area about two weeks ago, with a 10-year-old child, Hasham Khan, developing fever, sore throat and other symptoms on Nov 12.

stories.title: Sheikh Hasina seeks to return to Bangladesh on December 16 on state carrier
summary: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from more than two years of exile in India on December 16, her spokesperson told Reuters on Tuesday, though the government said she can only return through extradition.

Hasina has denied the charges from exile. “She can only return home by extradition treaty; in handcuffs, and under strict surveillance,” Humaiun Kobir, Bangladesh’s minister of state for foreign affairs, told Reuters.

A Bangladeshi minister told Reuters on Sunday that Hasina would be arrested and jailed on return and that there had been no official discussions with India about sending an aircraft to bring her back.

stories.title: KP's MNJ Road closed to traffic until next summer
summary: We have, therefore, restricted the entry of motorists and passenger coaches beyond Naran in Kaghan Valley,” District Police Officer Mohammad Waqas Khan told reporters here on Monday.
He said severe cold had gripped the valley following a fresh spell of snowfall earlier this month.
Meanwhile, the road connecting Naran with Saiful Muluk Lake remains closed.

stories.title: Digital gateway launched in Sindh for youth to access banking, education and jobs
summary: Speaking at the launch ceremony, the chief minister termed it a practical commitment to placing young people at the centre of the province’s development agenda. “The future of Sindh and Pakistan depends on the opportunities we create for our young people today.
He said the programme would bring together government departments, educational institutions, financial organisations and private sector to establish a comprehensive support system for young people.

He urged all provincial departments, public institutions and private organisations to become active partners, stressing that youth empowerment required collective efforts in education, skills development, technology, healthcare, sports and employment.

stories.title: 11 more ‘illegal’ Afghan nationals detained in Rawalpindi
summary: RAWALPINDI: Police in its ongoing crackdown rounded up 11 more Afghan nationals in the garrison city and shifted them to the refugee centre.
Later, the Afghan nationals, including seven women, were shifted to the holding centre for further proceedings.
A verification desk has also been established to collect details of the Afghan nationals brought by the police to the holding centre.

stories.title: Hyderabad Development Authority decides to auction nearly 1,000 plots despite objections by revenue officials
summary: The revenue authorities, the custodians of all state land intended for sale or mutation, have declined a request from HDA’s additional secretary to assess the price of the plots.

In a letter of Nov 17 to HDA’s additional secretary, written after fact-finding reports by the Latifabad and Qasimabad mukhtiarkars, the Hyderabad deputy commissioner questioned HDA’s legal authority to hold the auction.

The HDA’s additional secretary had written to the additional deputy commissioner-I, Hyderabad, requesting a “price assessment for plots auction of HDA’s housing schemes” and listing 991 plots in the two talukas.

stories.title: Capital Development Authority receives lowest bid of Rs14.6bn for new convention centre in Islamabad
summary: The SCO summit is likely to be held in August next year in Islamabad and CDA is going to overhaul the JCC besides constructing a new convention centre of a similar size adjacent to it.
CDA officials said the project will likely be completed in six months and the construction firm will hand over the centre to the civic agency on June 30.
Earlier, the CDA wanted to construct a mega New Islamabad Convention, Exhibition and Expo Centre (NICEEC) project near Malpur and also received bids of Rs37 billion.

stories.title: Growers body gives sugar mills three days to start cane crushing
summary: SUKKUR: Leaders of the Sindh Chamber of Food and Agriculture (Sukkur Division) have threatened protests and sit-ins outside sugar mills if sugar cane crushing does not begin within three days, accusing the agriculture department of negligence and causing heavy losses to growers.

The leaders said that if the mills did not start crushing and buy cane from growers within three days, they would stage sit-ins outside the mills and launch a campaign for the removal of the agriculture secretary.
The leaders urged the Sindh government to remove the secretary and the cane commissioner, take immediate notice of growers’ losses and “save the agriculture sector”.

stories.title: Punjab CM orders to double wheat, flour supply
summary: LAHORE: Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz has directed the authorities to double the supply of wheat and flour in a bid to bring down prices, warning of a crackdown on sellers charging excessive rates three days after the increase in supply.
The decision was taken at a meeting chaired by the chief minister to review the rising prices of flour and devise measures to stabilise the market.
She said the government would not allow market mafias to manipulate flour prices and reiterated its commitment to ensuring the availability of wheat and flour at affordable rates.

stories.title: 'Carrying hopes of 250m people': Zeeshan Ali to be first Pakistani in space aboard China's Shenzhou-24
summary: Zeeshan Ali was named a crew member of China’s Shenzhou-24 space mission on Tuesday, which is scheduled to launch on November 25, with Ali set to become the first Pakistani to undertake an orbital space mission.
According to the CMSA, the Pakistani astronaut will serve as a payload specialist during the mission and return aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft, which docked with the Tiangong space station in May.
Under the pact, two Pakistanis were to train in China, with one joining a mission on the Tiangong space station operated by Beijing.

stories.title: Primary schoolteachers hold sit-in near Bhuttos’ mausoleum in Larkana
summary: LARKANA: Hundreds of primary schoolteachers (PSTs) coming from five districts of Larkana division held a one-kilometre-long foot march from Naudero to Garhi Khuda Bakhsh Bhutto on Monday for the implementation of the service structure approved in 2021.

The protesters had travelled to Naudero from all parts of Larkana, Shikarpur, Jacobabad, Qambar-Shahdadkot and Kandhkot-Kashmore districts on a call for the march and sit-in given by the All Sindh Primary Teachers Association (APTA).
The APTA leaders said that considerable confusion prevailed among teachers over the biometric verification system.

stories.title: Not more provinces, but local bodies, will bring power closer to people
summary: https://www.dawn.com/news/2046704/the-missing-link

stories.title: The missing link
summary: RULERS who don’t bring power closer to people via strong local bodies want us to believe that they will now bring power closer to people via more provinces.
Would rulers who have kept local bodies so weak for so long empower new provinces?
The aim behind dividing provinces may be to make them powerless like local bodies and actually move power away from the people.

stories.title: Sindh govt won’t allow occupation of land vacated by Afghans, PA told
summary: KARACHI: The Sindh Assembly was informed on Monday that the provincial government would not allow anyone to occupy land vacated after the repatriation of a large number of Afghan nationals who had been living on Karachi’s outskirts for decades.
The issue was raised by the lone member of the Jamaat-i-Islami, Muhammad Farooq, during the Sindh Assembly’s Question Hour that pertained to katchi abadis.
CM’s aide Najmi Alam says all vacated land on city’s outskirts handed over to MDA “What is the current status of the Afghan settlements that have been vacated, particularly in Karachi?” he asked.

stories.title: Drug smuggler killed in ‘CCD encounter’ in Jhang
summary: On seeing the police, the suspects opened fire on the team.
RECOVERED: Jhang’s Satellite Town police recovered a kidnapped farmer and his seven cattle, collectively worth more than Rs5 million, during a raid in Sahiwal tehsil of Sargodha district.
He said police used modern technology to trace the suspects and recovered the abducted farmer and his cattle after arresting two alleged kidnappers, identified as Mumtaz and Ashraf.

stories.title: The question of new provinces — ruling allies delaying the inevitable?
summary: https://www.dawn.com/news/2046707

stories.title: Delaying the inevitable
summary: Within minutes, Atta Tarar, the information minister of the federal government that is yet to own the new provinces officially was on television, to criticise BBZ.
With their access to the hallowed halls of power, they are privy to some information on how the provinces may go forward, despite the resistance from the PPP.

That Atta Tarar defended this idea in his video talk that followed BBZ’s press conference means there is some truth to the matter; since then Rana Sana has also agreed that a referendum might be the way forward.

stories.title: Lahore ATC grants five-day remand of PTI leader
summary: LAHORE: An antiterrorism court (ATC) on Monday granted five-day physical remand of PTI leader Mian Usman Akram in the Askari Tower attack case of May 9 riots.
The investigating officer (IO) sought physical remand of the PTI leader, alleging that he was involved in the attack on Askari Tower.
ATC Judge Malik Abid Hussain allowed the police request and approved five-day physical remand of Akram.

summary: https://www.dawn.com/news/2046611

stories.title: LHC rejects US-Indian origin citizen’s plea for Pakistan Origin Card
summary: LAHORE: Dismissing a petition by an American citizen of Indian origin, the Lahore High Court (LHC) has ruled that marriage to a Pakistani citizen does not create an automatic right to seek a Pakistan Origin Card (POC).
Says marriage to a Pakistani doesn’t create an automatic right to seek Pakistan Origin Card A request for relaxation was declined by the authority, which he challenged before the court.

He noted that marriage under Rule 4(5) establishes threshold eligibility but not an entitlement as final issuance remains contingent upon mandatory verification and subject to Nadra’s statutory authority to refuse a card on grounds of national security or public interest.

stories.title: Used phone import surge hits industry
summary: ISLAMABAD: Imports of used smartphones surged from 1,434 units in July to 98,383 in October, as the duty gap between locally manufactured phones and imports narrowed.

The Pakistan Mobile Phone Manufacturers Associ­ation (PMPMA), in a letter, has raised concerns with the Ministry of Industries and Production and the FBR about the development, noting that the most alarming issue is the sharp increase in used smartphone imports.

PMPMA Chairman Abdul Rehman told Dawn on Monday that the surge in CBU imports is driven by two factors: narrowed import tariff gaps, which have fuelled the ‘khepia’ business, and a downward revision in FBR taxes on imported phone sets.

summary: https://www.dawn.com/news/2046658

stories.title: Civilisational dialogue
summary: WHENEVER representatives of Pakistan and India meet, even in multilateral settings, there is hope for a rekindling of ties.

But considering last year’s armed conflict between both states, and the ensuing toxic atmosphere in South Asia, it is a welcome development that Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik travelled to New Delhi recently for the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum.
Mr Malik said that he was in India for an SCO event; when the Indians would call him to discuss terrorism and other irritants, he would address these specifically, as Pakistan also had concerns.

stories.title: Journalists protest closure of media offices in Balochistan
summary: QUETTA: Journalists of Balochistan on Monday staged a two-day protest sit-in against the closure of 11 media bureaus and dismissal of a large number of journalists, at a protest camp set up in front of the Quetta Press Club.
The protest call was given by Pakistan Federal Union of Journalists.
He urged leaders of political parties, lawyers and civil society members to support the journalists.

summary: https://www.dawn.com/news/2046670

stories.title: Petroleum dealers warn of another strike over unmet demands
summary: KARACHI: The Paki­stan Petroleum Dealers Association (PPDA) on Monday warned that dealers would shut their petrol pumps unless the government fixes fuel prices for 30 days at a time, giving it 15 days to resolve the issue.
At the time, it wanted the dealers’ margin raised from 2.59pc to 8pc, after a Rs55 per litre increase in diesel and petrol prices.

In August too, the PPDA issued a 72-hour strike ultimatum, but backed down after the petroleum minister told a PPDA delegation that the government would continue the daily price-fixing mechanism, rejecting the dealers’ demand for monthly pricing.

stories.title: Plan to split Sui gas firms lands on PM’s table
summary: https://www.dawn.com/news/2046673/plan-to-split-gas-firms-lands-on-pms-table

stories.title: Plan to split gas firms lands on PM’s table
summary: The petroleum division has proposed at least four gas sales entities, with two competitive gas supply (CGS) companies for commercial and industrial consumers and two regulated gas supply (RGS) entities serving domestic consumers.

In SNGPL’s case, the transportation and CGS segments are projected to earn after-tax profits of Rs24bn and Rs36bn, respectively, while the RGS segment would post an after-tax loss of Rs158bn, with gas costs of Rs322bn far exceeding sales revenue of Rs224bn.
For SSGCL, the projections allocate the cheapest gas from low-cost fields (Rs328 to Rs876 per MCF) to the RGS segment — the most favourable scenario for domestic supply.

stories.title: Challan submitted in Hina Javed murder case
summary: RAWALPINDI: Police have submitted challan to the District Prosecution Branch in the murder case of Hina Javed after completing the investigation and incorporating forensic reports into the case record.
The district prosecutor has received the challan and initiated scrutiny.
Sources in the Prosecution Branch said if any legal deficiencies or shortcomings were identified during scrutiny, the challan could be returned to the police for rectification.

stories.title: Punjab CM to inaugurate 35 electric buses, review projects in Rawalpindi today
summary: PML-N Divisional President and MNA Malik Ibrar Ahmed told Dawn that the party finalised the arrangements to welcome its leader and chief minister in the city.
Security arrangements More than 4,000 police personnel will be deployed to ensure foolproof security and manage traffic during the chief minister’s visit to Rawalpindi.
As part of the security measures, the traffic police have made a traffic plan to facilitate the public during the visit of the chief minister as additional personnel will be deployed.

stories.title: NAB files reference in Rs37bn Kohistan corruption case
summary: PESHAWAR: The National Accountability Bureau, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, on Monday filed a reference in a high-profile case involving the alleged embezzlement of over Rs37 billion funds from the Upper Kohistan district accounts office.

An official said the reference comprised seven volumes containing 36,000 pages and named around 140 accused, including officials of the district accounts office and communication and works department, staff members of commercial banks and dozens of private contractors.

NAB alleged that the accused abused their official positions to initiate fraudulent withdrawals from the government treasury by creating forged documents, which were used to siphon off funds from bank accounts.

stories.title: SHC rejects pleas seeking transfer of corruption appeals to other forums after NAB law tweaks
summary: Notably missing is any procedure provided for transfer of the appeal or identification of authority competent to do so.” “For appeals, no framework in this connection has been identified.

Despite subjecting appeals to the transfer in the given amendment, the legislature has glaringly missed out to layout outlines to effect such transfer under,” the judges observed. “There is a deafening silence in this respect in law.

The object is to provide clearer, fairer, more effective rules, and better justice,” it added. “The legislature through an amendment could declare a judgement or an order as null, void or un-executable but cannot reverse it by substituting it for its own decision.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill UNRWA worker, two others in Gaza
summary: CAIRO/JERUSALEM: Israeli airstrikes killed at least three people in Gaza on Monday, including a man working for the UN Palestinian refugee agency UNRWA, the relief age­ncy and local health officials said.

Defence minister says police, not army, should handle settler violence Later on Monday, another Israeli air strike targeted a vehicle in western Gaza City, killing two people and wounding others, medics said.

Settler violence The defence minister in Israel’s caretaker government on Monday said the police, not the military, should deal with violent settlers in the occupied West Bank, after Palestinian vehicles and properties were torched over the weekend.

stories.title: Walkout over withdrawal of Fazl’s security
summary: QUETTA: Opposition members in the Balochistan Assembly staged a walkout on Monday to protest against the withdrawal of security guards provided to JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman.
Immediately after the session began, JUI-F MPA Zahid Reki rose on a point of order and drew the attention of the chair and members to the withdrawal of security provided to his party chief.
JUI-F, NP members return to Balochistan Assembly after ministers intervene Home Minister Ziaullah Langove said he was unaware of the details surrounding the withdrawal of the Maulana’s security.

stories.title: Islamabad hosts meeting of IAEA nuclear security network
summary: Effective nuclear security relies on strong national institutions, skilled professionals and sustained international cooperation, Hashmi said, as he reaffirmed the IAEA’s central role in the global security framework.

He highlighted the importance of human resource development in strengthening nuclear security and acknowledged the NSSC Network’s contribution to developing professional competencies and promoting international knowledge-sharing.

Shah noted that the Network has evolved into a valuable global platform for sustainable nuclear security capacity building, with Pakis­tan actively contributing to its obj­ectives through its national institutions.

stories.title: Punjab holds over 60pc of senior federal posts, Senate body told
summary: Expressing concern over the 60.17pc representation of Punjab in BPS 18-22, he stressed the need for equitable representation of the four provinces, particularly Sindh and Balochistan in the federal jobs.
Subcommittee demands strict enforcement of constitutional shares of four provinces in federal employment, natural resources “This rectification must be made immediately,” he said.

The subcommittee directed the Federal Public Service Commission (FPSC) to provide details of vacant posts and appointments from Sindh and Balochistan, while ensuring strict adherence to the prescribed provincial shares.

stories.title: Zeeshan Ali to be Pakistan's first astronaut in space aboard Shenzhou-24
summary: Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali is set to become the first foreign astronaut to visit China's Tiangong space station, joining the Shenzhou-24 mission crew scheduled to launch on Wednesday, the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) on Tuesday.
Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal congratulated Ali on his selection in a post on X, saying the mission reflected the trust and close ties between Pakistan and China.
The agreement marked a new phase in Pakistan-China space cooperation, providing for Pakistani astronaut training and participation in China's crewed space missions.

stories.title: Iranian parliament speaker says US seeks ‘no war, no peace’ stalemate with Iran, calls for deterrence
summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf said on Monday that the US wants to impose a "no war, no peace" stalemate on Iran, arguing that "sustainable deterrence" alongside or instead of negotiations is the way to end the threat of conflict.

The US and Iran signed a framework agreement in June to end hostilities and began negotiations, which later stalled amid disagreements over how to ensure safe and free navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.
The US and Israel launched a war against Iran on Feb.

stories.title: Smith eyes return to PGA Tour after LIV Golf collapse
summary: Cameron Smith admitted Tuesday "a lot of weight" had been lifted from his shoulders with the demise of LIV Golf and he was fired up to play on the European circuit, with his eye on a return to the US PGA Tour.
Smith, who joined LIV on a big-money contract a month after winning the 2022 British Open when he was world number two, said he eventually hoped to find a permanent home back on the US PGA Tour.
He can enhance his chances by at least gaining a full DP World Tour card by winning the Australian PGA Championship or next week's Australian Open in Melbourne.
